note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/screen100/{base_cue,sft025_cue,sft1_cue}-01/per_problem.json (committed in the repo, fields problem_index, score_v3, cap_hit, n_generated; 100 rows each, one per problem). First row per problem_index kept, restricted to the problem_index set common to all three. Main number: per-arm median of n_generated over that arm's rows with cap_hit false and n_generated present (cap-hit exclusion applied per arm independently, so the arms' medians may cover different problems); even count uses the mean of the two middle values; f = ln(M025/Mbase)/ln(M1/Mbase). If M(sft1_cue) <= M(base_cue) the script prints refuted_without_number, as the recipe says. refuted_by is null, so refuted_by_met is false otherwise. Alt reading (alt_measured): the same f but computed only on problems finished (cap_hit false) in all three arms, i.e. a paired exclusion; null if undefined there. Interval: bootstrap over common problems, each entry the (base, sft025, sft1) row tuple, the per-arm exclusion redone inside each resample; resamples where f is undefined are ranked as -inf, and an infinite endpoint is printed as null. Risks: excluding cap hits removes the longest answers, and if sft1 has many more cap hits than base its median is biased downward, which shrinks the denominator and can push f up (or above 1); the denominator can be small, making f unstable, and the bootstrap interval may be wide.
